rules.title: Prohibition on sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy
rules.requirement: The sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco is prohibited. An algorithmic device is a device, such as a software program, that uses algorithms to analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to give a landlord recommendations on what rent to charge for a vacant unit.
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
rules.interaction: Source says a tenant or the City Attorney may bring a civil action over a suspected violation. No interaction with state or other local law is stated.

warnings: The source is a Rent Board news notice and does not give the ordinance number or enactment date, so enacted_on is null.
The source states no exemptions or penalties. Exemptions are null, and coverage assumes residential units in San Francisco only.
The definition of algorithmic device given here is a summary. The full ordinance text should be checked for the exact definition, including how occupancy-level management is covered.
The civil action right for tenants and the City Attorney is described but not drafted as a separate rule, because it is an enforcement mechanism and not one of the six supplied categories.
